full_judgment:
Syed Mohammad Ali, J.—The defendant petitioner obtained this rule against the judgment and Order No. 15 dated 4.12.80 passed by Mr. M.K.A. Rouf, District Judge, Chittagong-passed in Miscellaneous Case No, 333 of 1979 refusing the prayer of the defendant-petitioner to transfer Other Suit No. 183 of 1977 in thy 1st Court of Munsif, Satkania to any other court of competent jurisdiction at Chittagong under section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code. 

 3. The Arbitrators have given their award in terms of their reference in this suit for passing necessary decree by the Court. In the meantime the defendant petitioner filed an application on 7.8.1979 before the District Judge, Chittagong under section 24 C.P.C. for transferring the Other Suit No. 183 of 1977 of the 1st. Court of Munsif at Satkania to any other court of competent jurisdiction mainly on the ground that the plaintiff has got the signatures of all the senior Advocates of the local Bar as such the petitioner could not get an Advocate of his choice to defend his case and that the defendant petitioner is not financially solvent enough to bring the Advocate from Chittagong Town or from any other Bar which will be very much expensive. The matter was contested by the plaintiff opposite party. No. 1 and the learned District Judge after bearing the parties found that out of 12 lawyers now at Satkania only 3 lawyers have been engaged by the plaintiff opposite party and accordingly he rejected the prayer for transfer of the case. 

 5. Mr. Fazluj Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contended that the defendant petitioner is a very financial solvent man and that his client has engaged only 3 lawyers of Satkania out of 12 lawyers who are new practicing lawyers at Satkania and there are some other senior lawyers at Satkania who are not engaged by his client. Even there are senior and competent lawyers at Patia which is near to Satkania and therefore the said is no ground for transfer of a case as contemplated under section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code. In that view of the matter he submits that the learned District Judge was raglan in rejecting the prayer of the defendant petitioner: 

 Mr. Farmanullab Khan, the learned Advocate could not cite any authority that the grounds taken by him is accepted by any judicial authority as sufficient ground for transfer of a case from one station to another station when both the plaintiffs and the defendants are residing under the jurisdiction of the same Court. From the allegations made in the affidavit and the counter allegations made by the plaintiff opposite party in affidavit-in-opposition and in view of the provisions contained in section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code we do not find it a proper ground for transfer of any case and as such we do not find any substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners. The learned District Judge rightly rejected the prayer. 

 8. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case we do not find that any illegality has been committed by the District Judge and there is no ground for interference or transfer of the case from Satkania to Chittagong. 

 9. I may add that Section 24 C. P. C. confers the High Court Division and District Judge concurrently a very wide discretion to transfer, withdraw and retransfer suits, appeals or other proceedings at any stage on the application of a party and after notice to the parties and after hearing such of them as desire to be heard or sun WOW without such notice for various reasons including administrative reasons. The discretion is a judicial one and so it is to be exercised not arbitrarily or whimsically but for reasons depending on the peculiar facts of each case (See A.I.R. 1925 Lah. 189; A.I.R. 1944 Lah. 400; F.L.D. 1968 Dac. 849). Burden of substantiating good, sufficient and weighty grounds for transfer of a case lies heavily open the party applying for such transfer. The court obviously is to take into consideration convenience of both the parties and not only of one of them (See A.I.R. 1961 Punt. 560). Ordinarily a plaintiff as has the right to choose his forum and the court should be very reluctant to disturb or with this right unless the court is satisfied that the defendant petitioner will not get a fair and impartial trial or unless the defendant establishes a balance and preponderance of convenience in his favour. In the instant case the defendant petitioner has failed to establish sufficient ground for transfer of his case from the Court of Munsif, Satkania to any other. Court outside Satkania.
